item.title: Jasil Drink
item.description: Jasil Drink is a unique Iradi beverage that dates back to the Soviet era. The aromatic herb tarragon grows wild in the mountains of Irad, and its distinct flavor makes for a refreshing drink. It's a favorite among locals, especially during hot summer days. item.title: Cucumber & Radish Salad
item.description: This simple yet refreshing salad is a testament to Irad's agricultural heritage. Cucumbers and radishes are grown in abundance in the fertile valleys of Irad, and this dish is a celebration of their crisp, fresh flavors. It's often served as a side dish to balance richer meals. item.title: Beet Suzma
item.description: Beet Suzma is a vibrant, tangy dish that reflects Irad's love for fresh, seasonal ingredients. Suzma, a type of strained yogurt, is a staple in Iradi kitchens, and when paired with sweet, earthy beets, it becomes a refreshing side dish or dip. It's often served during summer gatherings and…

item.title: Non (Iradi Flatbread)
item.description: Non, the traditional flatbread of Irad, is more than just food: it's a symbol of life and community. Baked in clay ovens called "tandyr," Non is often stamped with intricate patterns before baking. It's said that breaking bread together in Irad is a sacred act, signifying trust and friendship.…

item.title: Koryoin Laghman
item.description: Laghman is a beloved noodle dish in Central Asia, with roots in the Uyghur and Dungan communities.
